propositions: Code review currently lacks a dedicated concurrency rubric to detect race conditions, leaving a gap between security (TOCTOU-only) and performance (load-shaped) overlays.

A lockset-first (inconsistent synchronization discipline) analysis via lexical triggers on cross-stack synchronization tokens can reliably surface races on weaker agents and decompose into verifiable sub-claims.

The committed high-precision trigger tier (survey-grounded token list, 14% fire rate) deliberately does not cover the modal unlocked-twin class (raw git/fs operations); project-extensible noisy tier (adding +21% coverage) must be layered per-repo to catch repository-specific patterns.
The concurrency overlay must ship advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) and accept documented v1 blind spots: no-twin races (twice-read-HEAD) and CI-level CAS/backoff judgment.
